newsitem.title: FRANCE: German president begins state visit to France.
newsitem.headline: German president begins state visit to France.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog arrived in France on Wednesday for a four-day state visit designed to highlight the close friendship between the former enemies at the heart of the drive for close European union.
Greeted with military honours at Orly airport by Defence Minister Charles Millon, he was due to hold talks with President Jacques Chirac and attend a state dinner at the Elysee Palace.
"We want to stress the normality of French-German friendship," Herzog told journalists in Bonn on Tuesday.
The German president's role is largely ceremonial, while Chancellor Helmut Kohl regularly coordinates policies with Chirac to foster closer integration within the European Union.

This first state visit by a German leader to France since 1984 was timed, however, to underline the closeness of ties a few weeks before Paris and Bonn are to launch a joint proposal for reform of EU institutions to make it more effective in police, justice, foreign and defence policy.
Kohl and Chirac plan a Franco-German initiative before an EU summit in Dublin in mid-December, officials said.
Dividing his time between Paris and Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, Herzog plans to stimulate a Franco-German intellectual discussion on civil rights issues.
The high point of his stay in Bordeaux will be a visit to Chateau de La Brede, the birthplace of the French political theorist Montesquieu.

French and German intellectuals will debate the 18th century philosopher's contribution to European thought. He pioneered the principle of the separation of powers, a foundation of the rule of law in modern democracies.
While in Paris, Herzog is to speak at a conference on the influence of the values of the 1789 French Revolution on German unification and open an exhibition about Berlin at la Defense.
He will also meet National Assembly President Philippe Seguin, Senate president Rene Monory, UDF party leader Francois Leotard, Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin and Paris Mayor Jean Tiberi.
He will also meet Jewish community leaders and visit the Great Synagogue of Paris.
Herzog, a Bavarian Christian Democrat and former chief justice of Germany's Federal Constitutional Court, has been president since 1994.
